title: Tenki
description: Lying at the foot of a wooden utility pole and looking straight up it, the cables crossing over you, under building summer cumulus. Drag across and the hour moves: the sun goes round behind you on its real path for a late-July day in Tokyo, and the pole, the crossarm and the cables are lit by it, a warm key on the sunlit face and blue skylight in the shade, the terminator crossing the pole from the morning side to the evening side, cable shadows falling across it, the steel and the cable sheath catching the light. Toward evening the sun reddens through the air and the clouds take its colour.
intent: Factory reality technique 12, 'Tenki' (factory/reality/techniques.md): sky replacement with consistent relight, driven by one physical quantity, the hour. A sky matte that keeps the wires (thin-structure trimap, colour-line unmixing in linear light), the foreground decontaminated of its old sky, MoGe-2 normals and metric depth, and for each Poly Haven _puresky HDRI an SH9 irradiance plus its sun (direction, irradiance, angular spread). The photo's own light is divided out in colour, with the lens's veiling glare taken off first and the trunk corrected for what the global fit missed (tools/depth/bakes/tenki/oldlight.py), and the albedo anchored to weathered pole wood (~0.14). The hour sets the sun from a solar-position model (35.7 N, declination +20.5, the camera facing north, so the path stays behind and beside the viewer), its colour and strength from Kasten-Young air mass with the key held at a clear sky's ~5:1 over the skylight on a sun-facing face, and turns the sky's SH9 with it (dimming it and warming it round a low sun, the clouds taking the sun's colour); the foreground is Oren-Nayar under the sun with sun shadows marched in screen space through the depth map, GGX for the cable sheath and galvanised steel, and SH9 skylight times a street's sky-view factor. References: herb-refs 3 (utility pole against summer cumulus), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonic_lighting , https://graphics.stanford.edu/papers/envmap/ (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan, an efficient representation for irradiance environment maps), https://people.csail.mit.edu/alevin/papers/Matting-Levin-Lischinski-Weiss-CVPR06.pdf (closed-form matting, colour-line model), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_mass_(solar_energy) (Kasten-Young). ?sky=0..4 holds a recorded sky at the hour it was recorded (4, building cumulus, is the default), ?t=7..18.5 holds the hour, ?still=1 skips the reveal.

Sky matte by tools/depth/segment.py sky, then tools/depth/bakes/tenki/matte.py (enclosed sky pockets found by colour back-projection, edges unmixed on the colour line between local sky and local cable colour, in linear light); foreground decontaminated F = (I - aB)/(1 - a); normals, metric depth and focal length by MoGe-2 ViT-S (tools/depth/normals.py, MIT). Bake: tools/depth/bakes/tenki (prep, matte, light, export, pack); tools/depth/bakes/tenki/oldlight.py (the old light in colour, and its residual on the trunk: shade.webp, trunk.webp).
